headlines.summary: Eli Lilly reported that sales of obesity drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro surged again in the third quarter.
headlines.article_text: Eli Lilly (LLY) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Eli Lilly reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that blew past estimates and hiked its full-year sales outlook. Demand for its obesity drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro surged again and topped estimates for the quarter. Despite that strength, sales of its new GLP-1 obesity pill Foundayo, which launched in the U.S. in April, were under Wall Street's expectations for the quarter. In this article LLY Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 4:53 04:53 Eli Lilly CEO Dave Ricks on the obesity market: The room for expansion is dramatic Squawk on the Street Eli Lilly on Thursday reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that blew past estimates and hiked its full-year sales outlook, as demand for its blockbuster weight loss drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro soared again. Despite that strength, sales of its new GLP-1 obesity pill Foundayo, which launched in the U.S. in April, were under Wall Street's expectations for the quarter. The pharmaceutical giant now expects 2026 revenue to come in between $91 billion and $92 billion, up from a previous guidance of $85 billion to $87 billion. Lilly projects its full-year adjusted earnings will be between $35 and $36 per share, which compares with a previous outlook of $35.50 to $36.50 per share. The company said it raised the underlying profit guidance by $4.07 per share at the midpoint, but noted that it is offset by $4.57 per share in charges tied to deals in the quarter. The company's shares rose about 9% on Thursday. Lilly's massive diabetes and obesity windfall – and market share lead over chief rival Novo – shows no signs of slowing down, even as the company grapples with lower net prices in the U.S. The pharma giant is converting its massive profits into a dealmaking spree, most recently striking an agreement to buy Merida Biosciences to develop a new class of treatments for serious autoimmune and allergic diseases. Here's what Eli Lilly reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $7.48 adjusted vs. $6.26 expected Revenue: $24.40 billion vs. $22.61 billion expected Resilient demand for Zepbound and Mounjaro has helped fuel several strong quarters for Lilly despite lower prices for the medications in the U.S., which came after a drug pricing deal struck with the Trump administration last year. In a release, Lilly also pointed to expanded U.S. coverage for obesity care, referring to Medicare's decision to start covering GLP-1s for weight loss in July under a temporary pilot program. "This is a program that's really working," Lilly CEO Dave Ricks said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." "We're pleased with the early uptake and access, and I think doctors and patients are as well." Mounjaro's worldwide revenue rose 65% to $10.72 billion for the quarter, including U.S. sales of about $5 billion. That surpassed the $10.10 billion in worldwide sales and $4.79 billion in U.S. revenue that analysts were expecting for the quarter, according to StreetAccount. Mounjaro notably saw strength internationally, with sales outside the U.S. jumping 93%. Zepbound, which entered the market roughly three years ago, posted $5.35 billion in revenue for the third quarter. That's up 49% from the year-earlier period, as demand for the drug also rose while realized prices dropped. The vast majority of those sales came from the U.S. Analysts were expecting $5.09 billion in global sales for Zepbound, including $4.99 billion from the U.S., according to StreetAccount. The Eli Lilly logo appears on the company’s office in San Diego, California, Nov. 21, 2025. Mike Blake | Reuters Lilly's newly launched obesity pill, Foundayo, which won U.S. approval in April, took in $184 million in sales for the third quarter. That fell under analyst forecasts of around $229 million in sales, StreetAccount estimates showed. It marks the second earnings report that includes revenue from the GLP-1 pill, which is competing head-to-head with a rival oral drug from Novo that launched in January. Lilly is working to maintain its dominance in the booming market for GLP-1 drugs, with the company holding 63% share of the U.S. obesity and diabetes drug market in the third quarter, according to an earnings presentation on Thursday. Novo's market share in the quarter was 36.6%. Ricks told CNBC that he estimates 3% to 10% of eligible patients access obesity care in the U.S., but said the "room for expansion here of this market is dramatic." Lilly is at the front of that push, he added. Internationally, Lilly held 58.4% share of the market, while Novo had 41.6%, the presentation said. Eli Lilly's revenue in the U.S. climbed 34% to $15.1 billion. Lilly said it saw a 41% increase in volume — or the number of prescriptions or units sold — for its products, primarily for Mounjaro and Zepbound. That was partially offset by a 7% decrease in realized prices, primarily driven by Zepbound. Lilly's quarter was also boosted by a sales-based milestone payout of $410 million for its Type 2 diabetes medication Jardiance, related to the company's collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim. Sales outside the U.S. jumped 47% to $9.3 billion, propelled by a 76% surge in volume and partly offset by a 29% drop in realized prices. The pharmaceutical giant booked net income of $6.45 billion, or $7.22 per share, for the third quarter, which includes the $4.57 per share deal charges. That compares with net income of $5.58 billion, or $6.21 per share, a year earlier. Excluding one-time items associated with the value of intangible assets and other adjustments, Eli Lilly posted earnings of $7.48 per share for the third quarter. headlines.article_text: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17 billion Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points DoorDash will acquire Instacart for $17 billion, the companies announced Thursday. The deal unites two delivery giants under one roof, with DoorDash's focus on restaurants and Instacart's robust stable of grocery partners. Speculation about a deal has swirled since last week. In this article DASH CART Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 0:50 00:50 DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $65/share in cash & stock Squawk Box DoorDash will acquire Instacart for about $17 billion, the companies announced Thursday, uniting two delivery giants under one roof. DoorDash will pay $65 a share in cash and stock, an 11% premium to Instacart's closing price on Wednesday, and about 26% above Instacart's closing price on Oct. 22, the last trading day before reports surfaced of a possible sale. Shares of DoorDash jumped more than 8% in premarket trading following news of the deal, while Instacart traded near the flatline. The deal is slated to close at the end of 2027 or early 2028, the companies said. DoorDash expects to retain Instacart's brand, enterprise technology products and app once the deal closes. DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in a statement that grocery is "one of the hardest things to get right online." He pointed to difficulties around picking the right inventory and delivering perishable goods to customers' doorsteps without damaging them on the way. "Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day," Xu said. "Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery." Read more CNBC tech news AI build-out hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecasts Alphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of search As Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning business Hands-on with Apple’s first touchscreen laptop: Touch is totally optional DoorDash reported its third-quarter results alongside the deal announcement. Adjusted earnings per share were $1.06, beating the average analyst estimate of 84 cents per share, according to LSEG. Revenue came in at $4.62 billion, topping LSEG estimates of $4.56 billion. Marketplace gross order value, which tracks the total dollar value of orders on its platform, grew 36% year over year to $33.9 billion, beating consensus estimates of $33.6 billion. Total orders reached 993 million, up 28% from a year ago. Speculation of a deal has swirled since last week, when The Information reported Instacart was exploring a sale and had held talks with companies including Uber and DoorDash. On Monday, several outlets reported DoorDash was in advanced discussions to acquire Instacart and that the deal could value Instacart at about $17 billion. Sources familiar with the matter had told CNBC on Wednesday that the deal could be announced as soon as Thursday morning. Acquiring Instacart would give DoorDash a bigger presence in online grocery delivery. DoorDash got its start in food delivery, and since then, it has added more retailers to its marketplace, such as Sephora, Macy's , Staples and Anthropologie. It's recently made grocery a bigger priority, adding a stable of regional grocers after announcing a partnership with Kroger last year. headlines.title: Stocks making the biggest moves premarket: Alphabet, Caterpillar, Eli Lilly, DoorDash & more
headlines.summary: These are the stocks posting the largest moves in the premarket.
headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves premarket: GOOGL, CAT, LLY, DASH Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Check out the companies making the biggest moves in premarket trading: Alphabet — The Google parent dropped 11% after its third-quarter earnings showed the company posted negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion. Its core search revenue of $63.35 billion missed the $64.96 billion estimate from analysts. Total company revenue of $127.58 billion also missed LSEG expectations of $128.22 billion. Caterpillar — Shares slid 9% even after the company reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that beat the Street. The company earned an adjusted $7.20 per share on revenue of $20.68 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG expected a profit of $7.08 per share on revenue of $20.55 billion. However, sales for its construction industries business came in slightly below estimates. DoorDash , Maplebear — DoorDash announced it is acquiring the Instacart parent for $65 per share. That is an 11% premium from Maplebear's closing price on Wednesday. DoorDash also reported a revenue and EBITDA beat for its third quarter. Maplebear was up 4.8% before trading was halted, while DoorDash rose 7%. Eli Lilly — The Zepbound and Mounjaro maker handily beat expectations for its third quarter, sending shares 4% higher. Eli Lilly saw adjusted earnings of $7.48 per share, compared with the consensus estimate $6.26 a share, per LSEG. Revenue came in at $24.4 billion, topping the $22.61 billion expected from analysts. Marvell Technology , Lumentum — Lumentum shares jumped 5% after Bloomberg News reported, citing sources that the data center optics manufacturer was in talks to be acquired by Marvell. A deal could be announced as soon as next week, the report said . Marvell shares dropped more than 11%. Microsoft — The software giant rose 2% after the company reported a beat on the top and bottom lines for its fiscal first-quarter earnings. Revenue came in at $92.28 billion, ahead of the $90.69 billion expected by LSEG. Meanwhile, adjusted earnings of $4.89 per share was better than the $4.73 expected by analysts. Revenue in the mega-cap's key Azure cloud business grew 48% year over year. Shell — The oil major climbed 3.6% after it nearly doubled its third-quarter profit from the year prior to $10.81 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG were expecting $9.92 billion. Norwegian Cruise Line — The cruise operator jumped 9.5% following its beat on the top and bottom lines. Norwegian reported adjusted earnings of $1.12 per share, topping the consensus estimate of 93 cents, according to FactSet. Revenue was $2.95 billion, versus the $2.88 billion anticipated by analysts. Chipotle Mexican Grill — Shares gained nearly 8% after the burrito chain reported same-store sales that beat estimates. Same-store sales in the third quarter grew 2.1%, versus the 1.5% increase analysts polled by FactSet anticipated. ServiceNow — The enterprise software company tumbled 20%. Third-quarter adjusted profit of $1 per share missed the LSEG consensus expectation of $1.02 a share. Subscription revenue guidance for the fourth quarter ranged from $4.245 billion to $4.255 billion, while the FactSet consensus called for $4.25 billion. Fortinet — The cybersecurity company plummeted 25.5%. Non-GAAP gross margin for the third quarter came in at 79.6%, while analysts polled by LSEG sought 80.1%. Separately, top and bottom-line results beat the Street's expectations. Sprouts Farmers Market — The Phoenix-based grocery chain plunged 23% after third-quarter earnings per share, revenue and same-store sales all trailed analysts' consensus estimates, according to FactSet data. Harley-Davidson — Shares of the motorcycle maker dropped 5% following a revenue miss in its latest quarter. Harley-Davidson posted revenue of $964.0 million, falling short of the StreetAccount consensus estimate of $1.07 billion. On the other hand, adjusted EBITDA of $93.9 million topped the FactSet consensus of $78.9 million. Crocs — The footwear stock surged nearly 18% after Crocs posted third-quarter earnings that beat expectations, and issued stronger-than-expected current quarter guidance. It posted earnings of $3.69 per share, excluding items, on revenue of $1.04 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet anticipated earnings of $3.31 per share on revenue of $1.00 billion. eBay — Shares climbed more than 6% after the company reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter results. Revenue rose 14% to $3.2 billion, while gross merchandise volume increased 15%. Growth from Depop, accelerating GMV, and raised full-year guidance gave investors further confidence in eBay's strategy. Honeywell Aerospace — The aerospace company was down 4% even after raising its full-year outlook for pro forma standalone adjusted earnings per share, calling for $7.85 to $8. The company also announced an initial quarterly cash dividend of 40 cents per share. Carvana — The used car dealer climbed 8%. Carvana third-quarter revenue and adjusted EBITDA topped the numbers Wall Street had been expecting, and it said the Securities and Exchange Commission closed a previously disclosed investigation and would not take any enforcement action. CNBC's Darla Mercado, Fred Imbert, Sarah Min, Paulina Likos, Scott Schnipper, Deena Zaidi and Nick Wells contributed reporting.
